Reason to buy this game.  It's aesthetically enjoyable.  That's it.  Do not buy this for gameplay.

The visuals, music, sounds, stages, and character design are all reminiscent of classic martial arts movies.  This game is basically an homage to those movies and their cast.  I got this and the sequel as a package for less than $4 during the summer sale.  Easily worth it to enjoy looking at what you're doing on the screen.

The controls work fine.  The moves I intended to do come out without any real problems.  The gameplay is where this game falls short.  It feels like a bad 90s Mortal Kombat clone.  Hitboxes or stun doesn't feel consistent or intuitive.  Spacing or priority doesn't feel like much of a consideration.  

Don't get this game expecting polished combat.  But do get this to acknowledge the developer's passion and effort.  If you're hitting the opponent, appreciate how cool it looks.  If they are hitting you, also appreciate it.  If you have some fighting game experience, play around with moves and attempt combos and enjoy the view.   Or a casual player can button mash and enjoy a nice spectacle.

This game is overall enjoyable so I can honestly recommend it.

Shaolin vs Wutang offers like 6 or so game modes (the usual. Training, arcade, etc), like 50 or so characters (no joke, I don't even know how many there are but there's A LOT of them) and like 20 or so stages (majority are set in China).

It pays homage to all them classic Martial Art films of the 70's, 80's and 90's. The soundtrack is pretty cool and it really does capture it's vibes.

Each character uses a different fighting style and a different weapon. At first glance there are no copies but there are a few lookalikes with similar fighting styles but all of them play different from each other, when it comes to their movelist (you watch all of them perform diffferent stuff, that is). But the basic core of the gameplay doesn't really change. Even though it has a bit of strategy in it, it's, in the end, just a mash fest 9/10 times. So beware if you want more depth.

Graphics are rather odd but charming. Looks like it came straight from a smartphone store but it also looks like an upscaled Wii game, at the same time. If you apply the film grain filter and remove all the HUD everything ends up looking pretty artsy, almost realistic, though.

And it seems the game was made by a single individual, so there's that. Honestly, it takes real skill and real patience to deliver such a project, by yourself. So keep up with the great work, developer! We need more people like you in the industry without a shadow of a doubt!

Gostei bastante deste aqui! Ele coloca a aparência de atores famosos de filmes de ação, com a trilha sonora característica e mais as diversas técnicas de artes marciais. Os comandos e combos são simples de serem executados. Uma das coisas que mais legais é a "defesa dinâmica": quando você defende um golpe, o personagem executa uma esquiva animada como nos filmes do estilo. Gostei também que apresenta diversos modos de jogo, inclusive um modo "torneio" para você jogar com a galera no sofá. Tem 30 personagens com estilos de luta únicos!  Os gráficos dos personagens ainda se seguram para 2024, já os de alguns detalhes dos cenários estão batidos. Em algumas situações dá para sentir um pouco de input lag nos comandos (que não é ideal para jogos de luta). Senti falta de um modo online também. A última consideração negativa é em relação à dificuldade da CPU que não varia quase nada: jogando no "fácil" e "normal" não vi muita diferença (inclusive a dificuldade de alguns personagens podem variar muito). Em geral o saldo é positivo: não perca essa pérola.

I have never seen a more genuine love letter to classic martial arts cinema than this. It's jank. But it's fun. And the soundtrack immediately feels like I'm watching Enter the Dragon again. Inputs are simple. It's just here to let folks do cool moves that these mfs did in the movies. Basic punch, kick, and weapon autocombos that can lead into motion input specials, a dash, back to block, two-button super, yet interestingly, a three button grab that only goes forward. It's basic. But you don't really need anything more. It's a fun time, and honestly, it's a game I have wanted for a long time but never knew that it already existed. I love a lotta fighting games that have references to legendary martial arts movie stars, but I've always wanted a game that just... has them. And this does. It has every 70s and 80s martial arts movie protag and villain you can think of. It's even got ones from movies I hadn't seen yet, and now I gotta remedy that. Easily a recommendation with its already low asking price, even lower during sales.
